## Project Overview

This project examines how the criminal justice system decides when a young person is treated as a child and when as an adult, and what that decision looks like from the inside. I'm asking where the legal line is drawn, how race, age, gender, and offense severity shapes who ends up in adult court, and how young people charged as adults come to see themselves. I'm also considering how media and public narratives about young offenders compare with actual sentencing outcomes. The project will hopefully combine national and/or state data on disparities with research on adultification and public perception. I also plan to center a planned interview with my father's friend, who was charged as an adult at 17, alongside first person accounts from others. I plan to present it as a visual report that alternates short text with data visualizations.
